residual_risks: a launcher waits on launch.lock with no bound while a CLI start/restart/stop holds it (compose up ≤180 s per service, docker stop on restart, tenant provisioning; a build under the lock only when a reap removed the containers during the wait and the image is also missing)
a split restart stops the orchestrator before waiting for launch.lock, so its downtime includes that wait
the orchestrator start is not serialized against a reap's runtime-dir removal (at worst that start fails; it no longer writes into the runtime dir)
the orchestrator branch's own re-inspect under :7890 (pre-existing) treats an unreadable docker as no owner and falls back to the port probe
a SIGKILLed launcher counts as detached at its attach time: no idle grace after it dies (documented)

dir-only reaping: an ambiguous pair counts as no registry entry; needs a readable OK registry and automatic runs skip planning on an empty registry; runtime dirs created by init or the CLI pre-build carry no marker
duplicate concurrent builds possible (CLI pre-build, init, launcher detached build); the pid guard covers launchers only
dry-run restart shows running sidecars as already_running; a refused orchestrator stop can be dropped from a blocked split restart's report
doctor --repo, doctor --profile --repo and profile show --repo still load the caller's catalog (deferred, documented in the design amendments)
output-shape changes: reap --json gains state_only/dir_only; a split run's start-plan.json lists only the worktree services; orchestrator-only starts return runtime_artifacts: []
dead code carried over verbatim in lifecycle.py (… or True filters, an unreachable orchestrator branch, if not is_free(...): pass, identical already_running conditional)
lock-order evidence: the ABBA case has a real-flock test; other ordering tests use spies and the reap-interleaving tests replay a reap inside a patched lock
under the lock, write_runtime_artifacts still truncates and rewrites mcp.env and the override (a detached build started earlier may read a truncated mcp.env)
a removed worktree whose sidecars keep running can reappear as an empty directory through Docker bind mounts (dope-memory ./.dopemux), demoting worktree_missing to idle (still reaped after idle_s)
flaky/host-dependent tests: test_mcp_port_allocator sequential allocation (1/12 isolated here) and test_init_next_steps (real mcp init against the host :7890/docker) — pre-existing

cycle 1 residuals retained: second restart of the same backend within one proxy window needs /mcp reconnect; per-worktree mcp.env/compose.override reflect the last launched service; legacy projects stay on the shared ConPort store (D5 Option A); build.log shared per runtime dir
a state-only reap candidate that keeps failing (state_error on a corrupt lease file) is planned every run and can take the launcher's cap-of-1 slot (no docker call)
an unreadable build pid file excludes its instance from reaping until fixed (fail closed); a reused pid excludes it for at most build_timeout_secs
idle is measured from launcher attach/detach only: sidecars started by hand with the CLI and never attached are reaped after idle_s (design)
in the explicit `reap --apply`, the under-lock pair inspection can hold launch.lock for up to run_cmd's 180 s default if docker hangs, as docker stop/rm already could

an idle state-only pair whose only remaining state is a runtime dir (entries stopped, leases released) is finished only when the worktree is gone (by ruling: never delete a live worktree's build log on idle)

reap candidates of every kind are re-inspected under the lock (one bounded read-only docker ps -a per attempted candidate); a plan whose container set changed, or an unanswered inspection, is skipped as stale and re-planned next run

LEASE_ENVRC_MISMATCH no longer blocks a leased service's start (the worktree's existing lease wins over a differing env-file port; doctor still reports the mismatch); the env file is informational by design

the host's port-leases.json holds hundreds of released test leases (pytest tmp paths) from earlier suite runs that wrote to the real registry; pre-existing hygiene, candidate for `dopemux mcp leases reconcile`/owner cleanup
a `start --dry-run` allocates and persists leases (intended and test-pinned; since B7 it also re-leases unleased env-file ports) — an auditor may question a dry run that writes leases

a legacy or manual container running on the env-file port while this worktree's lease names another port makes `start` report already_running with registry ports the container does not publish (previously a blocking LEASE_ENVRC_MISMATCH); doctor still reports the mismatch; stop then start recreates the container on the leased port

the own-sidecar port guard trusts the 4-hex worktree_hash label; a collision between two worktrees of one project would let one adopt the other's published port (such a collision already breaks container naming and the runtime dir)

remaining_risks: Direct CLI `dopemux mcp start --service task-orchestrator` does not acquire `instance_lock` (by design, to avoid nesting `instance_lock` with `reserved_port_lock(7890)`), so a concurrent `reap --apply` on a removed/idle worktree can remove `runtime_dir` after the orchestrator registry update; `skip_artifacts = not compose_services` (src/dopemux/mcp/lifecycle.py:710) prevents recreating `runtime_dir`, leaving at most a stale orchestrator registry entry (documented in design.md:304).
`dopemux mcp doctor --repo <target>` and `dopemux mcp profile show --repo <target>` still load the caller checkout's catalog when invoked from outside `<target>` (documented in design.md:305).

Interactive `dopemux mcp switch-project` without `--yes` performs an unlocked pre-check before prompting the operator and re-verifies ownership under `reserved_port_lock(7890)` before mutating state (src/dopemux/commands/mcp_commands.py:432-477, documented in design.md:306).
